_why: Sites where an assertion judges a wall-clock reading in the machine-measuring direction (`elapsed() < bound`) and the min-of-K instrument could not be used. Every entry needs a `kind` from the table below and its own `note`; the scan prints the notes on every run so a reader can rebut them, and it fails on an entry that names a kind the table does not define. An empty list is the honest state: the three sites this scan found (REQ-A854 / F-DEV-109) are all bound through `fastest_of`, so nothing is excused here yet.

no-instrument-possible.reason: The measured quantity is not repeatable in-process: the first call performs one-time work (JIT-ish warmup, a lazily built table, a first-touch allocation) that later attempts do not, so the minimum over K would measure a different program than the one under test. The note must say which one-time effect, and the site should prefer a bound so wide that only a hang can cross it.
no-instrument-possible.note: Shape of a member: { "file", "line", "kind": "no-instrument-possible", "note": "…which one-time effect, and why the bound is a hang guard rather than a budget…" }

deliberate-machine-claim.reason: The test exists to decide something about the machine (a throughput floor, a hardware capability gate, a benchmark-derived calibration), not about the code's asymptotics. The note must say why the machine IS the subject.
deliberate-machine-claim.note: Shape of a member: { "file", "line", "kind": "deliberate-machine-claim", "note": "…why the machine is the subject here…" }
